# Audit 20 continuity review — 2026-09-22

Read-only repository/history review. The six required operating documents were accessed in order. Reviewed the audit/incident/retention corpus (30 Markdown audit logs plus evidence/reproduction artifacts), financial issue records, and later September 22 deployment continuation in OP_RETURN_INFRASTRUCTURE.md. No production checks or mutations were made for this review. Do not treat historical observations as fresh health evidence.

The companion predecessor-inventory.json hashes all current files in audits/ plus ID_REFUNDS.md, TREASURY_LEDGER.md, BUG_BOUNTY_LEDGER.md and both WORK refund JSON records. All 41 entries in Audit 19's predecessor inventory match current bytes and SHA256 exactly. All audit JSON parsed successfully. Audit 19 current MD SHA256: d9cc19784ce8fd72844fd4a8c92bc140bc49ee8fd2b688dd34de1e4de8479a1d. Original Audit 19 evidence: 63c83279344e99372a850eb02881147ea2a3f84afdf8f17431a774344cca5b96.

## Latest production state recorded before this audit

The September 22 continuation is OP_RETURN_INFRASTRUCTURE.md:3240–3407, not an appended Audit 19 section. It records successful bounded candidate retry6 at Core 968091/hash 00000000000000000001a9690637e05c0a683a1f5fe3452e69b4d8a04a846674; receipt SHA256 d3af60844e02df1b295911b18ae202c0ca28c3d0ebba7958aae7e05ccd841c0f. Application source matches the API candidate; intervening commits were runner/documentation changes. Public readiness reached 968106 after normal intervening blocks. This is a prior bounded pass, not this audit's result.

That rollout fixed embedded reboost content, historical action-signal presentation, owner-routed paid Boost interactions and selectable fee controls, and single document scrolling. Historical registry-paid 546-proof reboost action signal is not current-owner revenue. Current source also includes c77fcf2 (September 21) pending V8 wallet-capacity state correction. Root names name the replacing release, not necessarily contained release. Resolve every actual manifest before removal. Historical August manifests include removed paths and stale release identities. Phase2C removed 12 nonlive DBs +3 backup duplicates; phase2E changed keep14→keep7, removed six logical sets and expired old physical base/WAL while retaining latest. September14 removed22 node /opt stage copies (~4.5G), but later releases replenished them. Never replay old cleanup commands as a fresh target list. Previous restore clones and recovery incident artifacts need separate live-use/dependency/coverage classification; age alone is no proof of duplicate data. ## Limitations for the next audit log

Stored-population/Core parity is stronger than samples but still not discovery completeness across all raw historical blocks. Scalar transition continuity/flags is not independently reexecuting every large transition preimage. No finite current gate certifies every future math input, every account/UI local state, real signing or adversarial mempool/reorg lifecycle. New audit should state exact populations/checkpoints, failures and unreached stages, while preserving specific prior closures and original IDs.

19 of 21 local npm gates passed; two existing local verification gates now fail because their harnesses no longer match current source. Passed: Q16 precision, exact bond arithmetic, marketplace V2, AMO V5/V6/V7/V8 and V8 gates, canonical order, INCB range witness, INCB oracle restore (28 checks), Audit19 accounting, index recovery (529/529 behavior checks), ID-audit contract, live-data, UI, Boost regression, send-prep fixtures (8), worker containment and read projections. Separate direct execution confirms 30/30 actual Boost tests, 5/5 read-projection tests, and 4/4 canonical-transfer-fee tests.

Independent seeded integer checking passed 262,170 assertions across 16,384 generated inputs (seed 0x9e3779b9). Checks execute actual frontend and server functions against independently expressed integer identities: Q16 decimal parse/format parity, exact Q8→Q16 conversion, V8 floor and minimum-price ceiling inequalities, valid face and supply boundaries, one-subatom terms, direct network-rational movement values, Q8/Q16 movement equivalence, Q8 decimal roundtrips, and WORK floor-value helpers. One initial checker return-type assumption (string vs BigInt) was corrected; it was a harness error, not a product finding. Finite deterministic vectors are not an exhaustive historical replay.

## New verification-gate regressions

- `check:work-precision` exits 1: `ReferenceError: tokenRequiresCanonicalWorkCapacity is not defined` at check-work-precision-contract.mjs:513. Its isolated VM globals at :201–215 omit current transitive dependencies added to tokenWalletBalancesFor at App.tsx:11224 by H19-04 commit 56694a7d. The run aborts before completing its former 131-check gate. H19-specific actual frontend/transitive-function tests pass separately. Source correction should update this harness with real dependencies and current authority-qualified fixtures; do not restore old wallet arithmetic or mock away capacity admission.
- `check:api-truth` exits 1 at its Boost signal assertion (:677–693). Eight of nine subpredicates pass; the sole failing regex expects `const proofSignalQ8 = boostExactQ8(...)`. Current source :52726–52736 correctly separates baseProofSignalQ8 and accumulatedOwnerSignalQ8 before adding exact WORK value (change 661e5764). All 30 actual Boost behavior tests pass. Replace the stale structural expectation with current exact behavior/owner-signal assertions. This failure is a verification-maintenance gap, not demonstrated incorrect production ranking math.

Both findings need separately approved test-code edits. Neither justifies changing canonical balances or records.

## Prior issues rechecked

- H19-01/H19-04 are already production-closed for their specific defects in Audit 19. Current local exact aggregate/capacity, one-unit boundary, stale checkpoint, missing evidence, replay reservation, pending deduplication, actual frontend, and preflight fixtures pass. This does not replace a newly pinned production response/transition comparison.
- Existing Audit17/Audit19 Boost writer-input validation lead still reproduces using actual isolated writer functions: price 1.9 becomes 1; payment 0.9 becomes 0; output index 1.9 becomes 1. Source anchors: boostProtocol.ts:348, boostWallet.ts:447/:466. Preserve prior issue identity. Validate original inputs as safe integers before normalization; no paid transaction was created or observed.
- V7 checks are historical compatibility/fail-closed coverage, not activation authority. V8 remains the active declared Q16 era and 25,000-proof face.

## Documentation inconsistency

MARKETPLACE.md:1346–1364 and :1427–1438 retain stale claims that seal5 can spend the original ticket without closing it and that a slow fresh summary should avoid 503. Current README and earlier Marketplace rules correctly require an unspent original ticket; exact fresh truth fails closed when unavailable. Qualify those dated sections as superseded and reconcile the unqualified Spent Ticket Closure section in an approved documentation change. No runtime discrepancy is inferred from these old words. The 16/18 MiB versus later runtime budget discrepancy is already documented in Audit 19; do not assign a duplicate issue.

## Limits and receipts

The supplementary `check:credit-mint-regressions` command was identified as a live HTTP check and failed immediately on local sandbox DNS `EAI_AGAIN credit.proofofwork.me`; no successful production read occurred. Treat unavailable, not application failure. Do not include it among 21 local gates.

This contribution performs no independent genesis-to-tip replay, live SQL population check, full-node declaration recheck, or connected-wallet signing test. Those require the parent audit's distinct receipts. ProofOfWork Core validates carrier chain facts; application-specific balances and value also require deterministic protocol replay.

All logs, the independent checker and result, the known-Boost recheck, source revision, sizes, and SHA256 receipts are under `/tmp/pow-audit20-local-math-20260922/`. `manifest.json`, `results.json`, `supplemental-results.json`, and `direct-results.json` index them. # /usr/lib/systemd/system/pg_basebackup@.service
[Unit]
Description=Basebackup of PostgreSQL Cluster %i
AssertPathExists=/etc/postgresql/%I/postgresql.conf
Wants=postgresql@%i.service
After=postgresql@%i.service
RequiresMountsFor=/var/backups/postgresql

[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=postgres
Environment="KEEP=3"
ExecStartPre=+/usr/bin/pg_backupcluster %i createdirectory
ExecStart=/usr/bin/pg_backupcluster %i basebackup
ExecStart=/usr/bin/pg_backupcluster %i expirebasebackups $KEEP

# /usr/lib/systemd/system/pg_basebackup@.timer
[Unit]
Description=Weekly Basebackup of PostgreSQL Cluster %i
AssertPathExists=/etc/postgresql/%I/postgresql.conf

[Timer]
OnCalendar=weekly
RandomizedDelaySec=1h
FixedRandomDelay=true

[Install]
# when enabled, start along with postgresql@%i
WantedBy=postgresql@%i.service

# /etc/systemd/system/pg_basebackup@16-main.timer.d/override.conf
[Timer]
Persistent=true

import os,pathlib,pwd,subprocess,sys,urllib.parse,json,datetime
gate=sys.argv[1]
scripts={'parity':'scripts/check-proof-indexer-parity.mjs','ids':'scripts/audit-id-registry.mjs','events':'scripts/audit-computer-events.mjs','ledger':'scripts/audit-ledger-consistency.mjs','mail':'scripts/check-mail-regressions.mjs','market':'scripts/check-marketplace-regressions.mjs'}
assert gate in {*scripts, 'semantic'} and os.geteuid()==0
pid=subprocess.check_output(['systemctl','show','proofofwork-api','-p','MainPID','--value'],text=True).strip()
current=dict(x.split(b'=',1) for x in pathlib.Path('/proc/'+pid+'/environ').read_bytes().split(b'\0') if b'=' in x)
root='/opt/proofofwork-api'
commit=subprocess.check_output(['git','-c','safe.directory='+root,'-C',root,'rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip()

**Window:** 2026-09-22 06:14:12–06:25:12 UTC. **Host:** `pow-bitcoin-01`, `65.108.122.87`. No production changes, removals, restarts, backups, restores, signing or broadcasts. No repository files edited. Parent agent covers primary PostgreSQL, full stored-population reconciliation and the UI VPS.

## Health and capacity

## Storage growth and one-backup retention request

Continue **H8-05/H10-02** and **H5-03/H10-03/A11-06**, not new duplicate findings. PostgreSQL backups now occupy about **120.44 GB**, versus 62.73 GB in H19. Latest installed trend (06:02:52) estimates **21,497,292,990 B/day** and **1,098,306 seconds / 12.71 days to the 100 GiB reserve** from one day's net use. This is a warning estimate, not a guaranteed deadline; backup/release bursts and growth can consume reserve sooner. Release allocation **12,499,173,376 B** exceeds its 8 GiB review threshold. Storage/trend/release monitors remain failed for their documented warnings; they were not reset.

User wants **one last verified backup/rollback per recovery purpose**. Current installed policies differ: managed node archives keep **3**, logical backup keep **7 is review/preserve-only**, weekly physical backup keep **3**. Release prune timer is explicit **dry-run**. No policy changed.

## New finding candidate: mempool frontend logs consume node root

`mempool-web-1` stores **3,800,495,351 logical B** in regular nginx app logs: `/var/log/nginx/access_mempool.log` **3,702,995,788 B**, actively updated; `error_mempool.log` **97,499,563 B**. These use the container writable layer on the **node root** filesystem, bypassing stdout/stderr and the monitored host `/var/log` allocation category. No rotated members appeared. The container has a daily/rotate-52 logrotate rule, but no observed cron process, expected daily runner or root crontab; host rules do not cover nginx/docker. Configuration alone does not prove rotation executes.

All three containers use Docker `json-file` with empty options (no observed `max-size`/`max-file`), although their Docker JSON logs currently total only about 12 MB. Node root has ample current headroom; this is persistent uncontrolled growth, not an imminent root-full claim. No matching nginx/container-log growth finding was found in prior audit Markdown search; parent history review should assign the final issue ID.

**Recommended correction requiring approval:** executable bounded rotation, or nginx stdout/stderr plus bounded Docker logging. Preserve required operational evidence before any removal/truncation. No remediation performed.

## Log health and auxiliary MariaDB

48-hour aggregate scans: kernel 12,824 entries; system warnings 14,802; API/worker 535,324; Core/Electrs 12,320. **Zero matched OOM, I/O-error, corruption, ENOSPC/disk-full, deadlock-detected or PANIC phrases.** Keyword counts are not unique incident counts. Kernel warnings mainly firewall blocks; Electrs warnings include peer disconnects and unavailable headers. PostgreSQL current 15.76 MB file scanned: mostly audit SQL syntax/column errors, plus statement timeouts and lost clients; no physical-corruption heading.

Current API/worker invocation (05:43:54–06:19:57, 6,044 journal entries) still logged **63 raw-RPC QUEUE_FULL, 3 incomplete canonical-order, 1 wallet-unavailable, 1 listing-lifecycle timeout**, and 30 disappeared-mempool transaction reads. Continue the existing readiness/latency family. Historical failed audit/cutover oneshots remain evidence; no serving-service crash inferred from those monitor states.

Auxiliary `mempool-db-1` MariaDB **10.5.21**, healthy/no OOM, checked **06:25:12 UTC** using internal credentials never printed. Read-only transaction and ten-second statement bound: schema `mempool` has **24 tables, all InnoDB**, estimated **285,343 rows**, catalog data **111,886,336 B** plus indexes **32,129,024 B**; `/data/mempool/mysql` allocation **413,581,312 B**. Catalog free extents **22,020,096 B** are not claimed reclaimable. Largest tables: blocks ~86.39 MB and statistics ~52.53 MB including indexes.

Zero sampled active InnoDB transactions, pending reads/writes or row-lock waits; cumulative deadlocks/log waits/table-lock waits/slow queries **all zero**. Four connections, lifetime max five, configured maximum 151. Buffer pool 128 MiB is fully occupied; **166 physical reads / 374,179,005 logical requests** and no observed I/O wait do not indicate pressure merely because free cache pages are zero. `innodb_checksum_algorithm=full_crc32`, `innodb_force_recovery=0`, file-per-table on. Last 48-hour Docker database log read succeeded with **zero lines**, `log_error` uses stderr. These counters are cumulative over 11,670,348 seconds uptime.

No CHECK TABLE, full table/page scans, repairs, flush, ANALYZE, auxiliary DB backup or restore were run. InnoDB tables were not given a speculative QUICK check without a proven bounded cost. Catalog/health/checksum configuration cannot certify every physical page or row, and estimated row counts are not exhaustive exact counts. No new primary-PostgreSQL physical/off-host restore, roles/grants restore or complete WAL-gap certificate was produced. Preserve the last restore-proven recovery set until its replacement is proven.
